summary: One Run, one machine that does not exist yet, and the two moments a start latency is the difference between. Placement answers for the cheap listing, and answering it is now an act: Mercator mints the lease and the node identity, hands the provider a bootstrap, and waits. Five minutes later the machine has been allocated, has booted, and its agent has opened a session, and only then is there anything to launch a workload on, so the launch is accepted at the moment Mercator next looks and not before. What follows is the part of the wait the workload owns: an eighteen gigabyte image crosses the link, and the container begins about two hundred and eighty-eight seconds after the machine took the work. That subtraction is what this fixture states. Ten minutes in the launch has been accepted and no container has started, which the record says as an absence rather than as a start borrowed from the acceptance; ten minutes after that the host reports the moment its process began and the difference is a measurement rather than a prediction. The provisioning the machine spent is not in it, because it is three stages of its own with three actuals of their own, measured between a provider that answers for the allocation and a registry that answers for the agent.
